Team — ran a quick back-of-envelope based on our tuned LLM runtime (continuous batching + KV cache for multi-turn). Assumptions: average generation per request 180 tokens, effective batching factor 2.8 during peak, sustained generator utilization target 70%.

Per-GPU baseline (approx):
- H100 80GB (optimized kernels): ~1,250 tokens/sec sustained (generation-only, single instance measured).
- A100 80GB: ~900 tokens/sec sustained (same config).

Sizing to hit 650M tokens/month (monthly seconds ~ 2.592M):
- Required sustained tokens/sec (avg across month) = 650,000,000 / 2,592,000 ≈ 251 tokens/sec.
- Allowing for 2.5x headroom for peaks and burst windows -> target capacity ~630 tokens/sec sustained peak capacity.

GPU pool options (latency-first vs cost-first):
1) Latency-first (H100 focus):
- Target pool: 1x small control plane + 6 x H100 80GB reserved (active).
- Nominal sustained capacity: 6 * 1,250 = 7,500 tokens/sec (plenty of headroom for burst & autoscale).
- Estimated Redwood reserved list price (before enterprise discounts): $/hour per H100 ~ $35 (placeholder), blended compute amortized cost mapping to $/1M tokens ≈ $220. With enterprise 12-mo commit discount (typical band) we can get to ~$165/1M.

2) Cost-first (A100 mix):
- Target pool: 8 x A100 80GB reserved.
- Nominal sustained capacity: 8 * 900 = 7,200 tokens/sec.
- Estimated blended $/1M tokens ≈ $160 at list; with a 12-mo commit discount band could approach ~$120/1M.

3) Minimal-risk starter (ramp-friendly):
- 4 x A100 reserved + 2 x shared burst H100 on-demand for 6–12 week ramp.
- This lowers committed spend upfront and lets us validate the traffic shape. Modeled blended $/1M ≈ $180 for first 3 months, then reprice at scale.

Notes & open questions:
- The $/1M estimates above are compute-only (GPU + infra); they exclude storage, networking, and support/observability add-ons. Add ~10–18% for full platform bundle.
- If procurement insists on a blended $500/1M target we are well below that on these options — leaving margin for discounts or more aggressive SLAs.
- We should propose two named SKUs (H100-latency and A100-cost) with explicit burst rules and an ability to swap instance types at renewal.

I’ll attach the micro-bench CSV (latency-profiles-A100-H100.csv) and a short table for pricing bands.
